purpose: First-quarter wave slice for the eighth Ruleset Card — the first card whose §1.3 identity ships NO dominant-verb line at all, authored onto Scale via the ratified ADR-0005 per-tier roster (ADR-0013 decision 14; 8 of the 20-type launch canon, OD-14(a)). Slice shape mirrors the seven shipped g1 siblings: a probe-drizzle opening on a board that only sparkles, the tenant's own burst as the surprise-with-composition beat (the catastrophe wears an API key, not a hood), a hollow-quiet trough where the enemy is the idle warmth still billing, and a finale built on the line's authored cruelty ('a recursive function that invokes itself and bills you $40,000 in nine minutes' + 'cost can be attacked without touching availability', §1.3/§2.12). Deliberately RULES-FREE (no rules block): §2.24 rule-carrier values stay in the g1 slices until the batch-D rule-adapter pass reads them for cross-type tables.

waves.title: key.wave.1
waves.note: Rule (b) honoured: first wave of any level ALWAYS <=40% of par (§1.7). Cold Start Minute governs the first 90s of sim-time: handover no threat, one FREE conversion, signature constraint asserts harmlessly with telegraph (§1.9). On this line the harmless assertion is a drizzle of probes walking published function endpoints while the pan is still cold — the quarter opens with the board sparkling quietly at a stranger who is the only party currently paying attention to it (§1.3's mayflies, §0.3's app-dev customers still asleep).

waves.title: key.wave.2
waves.note: Rising floor beat one — the ROUTINE catastrophe, and it is a customer succeeding. Two-Front (§2.24): the single tenant whose burst starves the pool (Parasite — 'a single tenant's burst starving others', §1.3 verbatim) spends concurrency on the shared shell, while the heavy invocation (Debuffer — one hot function reading everything, §2.12's DBaaS sibling: 'One tenant's unindexed analytical query starves everyone else's transactions') spends cash on the pool you refused to pre-warm. Everyone else's mayflies pay for a stranger's success — the arrival-history law as a fairness lesson.
waves.entropyNote: entropy budget here = f(estate age x size x (1 - maintenance spend)), NOT wave number (§2.24) — on this line maintenance spend IS pool warming, and the card prices it twice: 'buying warmth is buying the absence of a stutter' as the purchase, idle warmth still billing as the unforgiven version (§1.3/§4.9).

waves.title: key.wave.3
waves.note: Rule (c): 30% is 50% below the preceding peak (60%) — >=45% satisfied. Dips are where the player builds (§1.7): the chrysalis pool, the share split, the timeout budget all get their window here. But on the serverless line the quiet is the bill: scale-to-zero is the reward for the pan going cold, and un-thought warmth costs idle money anyway — 'Costs idle money for latency you only notice by its absence' (§4.9 verbatim). Two fronts: hands x cash — the Sapper's held-open shells read as headroom while the meter climbs for warmth nobody summoned.

waves.title: key.wave.4
waves.note: Compound-wave exemplar, serverless variant: a bad dependency-layer push walks the fleet (Splitter debuts here, the every-4th-wave NEW ROLE beat; unseen in waves 1-3, the registry's only purchased-batch mechanic reused per this line's threat-mapping law) — every cold start on the board turns a shade duller — and inside the same window one function finds its own endpoint and starts recursing (Parasite — 'a self-DDoS with a bill attached', §4.9 verbatim), because a fleet mid-stutter is exactly when the timeout budgets nobody tuned get their audit. Two fronts: concurrency (the pool choking on frost) x cash ('cost can be attacked without touching availability' — tonight it is only attacked).
waves.secondIncident: runaway recursion arrives inside the batch-stutter incident window -> 1.8x multiplier applies (stated openly in the Codex, §2.24).

waves.title: key.wave.5
waves.note: The finale is the line's sparkle going dark: the herd arrives against the pool the batch push just chilled (Parasite carry — the starver from wave two is structurally back, §3.1's law now obvious to the player), held-open shells keep sipping shares (Sapper), and one tenant's table-scan-heavy function spends the last of the warm capacity (Debuffer) — the shimmer field fills with dark specks, 'holes in the sparkle' (card verbatim), and every hole is somebody's first visit. Hard wave draws TWO fronts — cash x reputation — per §2.24: the runaway invoice and the app developers whose cold openers blamed YOUR uptime page. Win check: the warm hold stayed smooth enough that nobody filed the ticket that names the stutter, while the meter stayed boring.
waves.triageWindow: after any catastrophic failure in this wave: arrivals queue visibly outside, patience draining, hands freed 30s (§1.7).
